title: Array Memory Layout
concept: An array is like an apartment building with units packed tightly together in memory

steps.title: Including stdio.h Header
steps.explanation:
Standard I/O header for using `printf`.

This lesson verifies through address printing that array elements are stored contiguously in memory.

steps.title: Starting the main Function
steps.explanation:
The main stack frame is created and the array `arr` is placed inside it.

An array allocates a contiguous block of "element count x type size" bytes all at once.

steps.title: Array Declaration and Memory Allocation
steps.explanation:
`int arr[3] = {10, 20, 30};` stores 3 integers in contiguous memory.

The key point is that the spacing between elements is always `sizeof(int)`, and this regularity is the foundation for pointer arithmetic.

steps.title: Address of the First Element
steps.explanation:
`&arr[0]` prints the starting address of the array.

The array name `arr` behaves like `&arr[0]` in most expressions, so you can calculate the remaining element addresses from here.

steps.title: Address of the Second Element
steps.explanation:
`&arr[1]` is `sizeof(int)` bytes greater than `&arr[0]`.

This follows the rule: `&arr[n] = &arr[0] + n * sizeof(int)`.

steps.title: Address of the Third Element
steps.explanation:
`&arr[2]` is also a contiguous address calculated by the same rule.

Since arrays are stored contiguously, accessing an index out of bounds is very dangerous.
steps.stdout:
arr[0] Address: 0x1000
arr[1] Address: 0x1004
arr[2] Address: 0x1008

steps.title: Program Termination
steps.explanation:
`return 0;` terminates the program and the array memory on the stack is cleaned up.

Key point: array elements are laid out contiguously, with address gaps equal to the type size.

quiz.question: For double arr[2]; if &arr[0] is at address 100, where is &arr[1]?
quiz.explanation:
`double` is typically 8 bytes.
Since arrays are packed tightly, the next element is at 100 + 8 = address 108.

misconceptions.wrong: You can change the array size later
misconceptions.correct: Basic arrays in C have a **fixed size**.
misconceptions.why:
At declaration, exactly that much space is allocated on the stack.
To resize, you need `malloc` and `realloc`.

keyTakeaway: Array elements are packed tightly together. The address difference between elements equals the type size (sizeof).
